scope: All 120 units read (dhyāna verses, the 108 verses of names, closing verses): text for sense, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page. The names are explained after Śaṅkara’s commentary.

items.issue: khaṇḍaparaśu was “wielder of the broken axe”; the axe is so called because it cleaves (khaṇḍana) the foe, as the gloss has it.
puṇyopetam was glossed “attended by the virtuous” against the translation’s “endowed with all merit”.
saptaidhāḥ was glossed “of seven flames”; edhas is fuel, as the translation says.
items.change: Gloss now “of seven kinds of fuel”.

items.issue: For some forty names the sentence translation and the word gloss give different explanations, both traditional (most are alternatives in Śaṅkara’s commentary). Examples: rudraḥ “remover of sorrow” / “who makes all weep at the end”; janārdanaḥ “the refuge sought by people” / “who afflicts the wicked”; pavanaḥ “the wind” / “the purifier”; dāśārhaḥ “worthy of offerings” / “born in the Daśārha line”; vīrahā (v. 99) “who ends the round of births”. A reader comparing the two layers will see them disagree.
options: A. Leave as it is: the two layers together show both explanations.
B. Make the word gloss repeat the translation’s sense everywhere.
C. Keep both, but add to the page note one sentence saying that where the two differ, both are traditional explanations.
items.recommend: C: it keeps the information and removes the appearance of error.
